runs.text: PENN's reported leverage fell through 2026 on the company's own definition. Total debt over LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is 2.58x against 3.50x at FY2025, and net debt over EBITDA is 1.62x against 2.67x, as cash rose to USD 1,044.8 million and EBITDA rose to USD 1,088.2 million from USD 830.1 million [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. The measure is management's non-GAAP view struck after triple net operating lease rent and it leaves out USD 4,359.4 million of financing obligations and finance leases, so an extended perimeter that adds them gives net leverage of 5.63x [CP-1 Calculations]. Creditors should therefore treat the improvement as real but read the level against the landlord claims, not against the headline ratio.

Liquidity is the clearest strength. Cash of USD 1,044.8 million plus an undrawn revolver of USD 976.1 million gives USD 2,020.9 million, against USD 432.3 million of debt maturing in the next twelve months and no committed facility located that expires within that period [CP-1 Chart data: liquidity; CP-1 Calculations]. The 2026 refinancing extended the revolver and Term Loan A to April 2031 and Term Loan B to May 2033 and added USD 600.0 million of 6.75% notes due 2031 [CP-1A Transaction summary and new debt issues]. The near-term maturity that remains is the USD 400.0 million of 5.625% notes due January 15, 2027, which the company classifies as long-term on its intent and ability to refinance.

The earnings recovery has two unequal sources. Retail Segment Adjusted EBITDAR was USD 501.8 million in Q3 2026 against USD 465.8 million, with the margin at 33.7% against 32.8% [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics]. The online segment's loss narrowed to USD 18.3 million from USD 76.6 million, but revenue excluding the gaming tax gross-up was USD 157.0 million against USD 158.2 million, and online gaming revenue fell, so the gain came from lower marketing, general and administrative and labor costs after the ESPN agreement ended [CP-1; CP-1A Company and operating model]. That makes part of the earnings recovery depend on keeping costs low.

Fixed charges remain heavy. LTM cash paid for interest of USD 382.4 million gives cash interest cover of 2.85x on LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, up from 2.17x at FY2025 [CP-1 Chart data: interest cover]. Leases are the structural issue: the AR PENN and 2023 Master Leases are cross-defaulted and a master lease default could trigger a default under the debt agreements, and the development funding GLPI provides adds annual rent of about 7.9% of the funds received [CP-1A Credit translations]. Covenant headroom is not measurable: the maximum total net leverage of 4.50x and minimum interest coverage of 2.00x are printed but the reported ratios and definitions are not supplied [CP-1 Covenants].

cells.text: Operates in 28 jurisdictions with casinos, racetracks, online sports betting (OSB) and iCasino; owns, manages or has interests in 42 gaming and racing properties in 19 states at 2025-12-31; five reportable segments: Northeast, South, West, Midwest, Interactive
Geographic spread reduces single-property risk; regional markets are mature and competitive, so cash flow depends on same-store spend.
Retail segments earn from slot machines and table games, food and beverage and hotel; slot machines were approximately 86% of gaming revenue for both nine-month periods
Slot-heavy gaming revenue is discretionary consumer spend, so revenue follows visitation and spend per visit; no contracted revenue floor.
Total revenues 5476.4: retail segments 4415.2, Interactive 1056.0 (of which gaming tax reimbursement 562.7), Other 14.8, eliminations (9.6)
About four fifths of revenue is retail; Interactive revenue is inflated by pass-through tax, so economic scale is smaller (493.3 excluding it).
Retail Segment Adjusted EBITDAR 1490.4 for nine months 2026 on revenue 4415.2; Q3 2026 margin 33.7% against 32.8% a year earlier
Retail EBITDAR is before rent; rent of 494.4 for nine months (operating leases) is then deducted to reach Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of 862.4.
Management states retail delivered "better than expected revenue and Adjusted EBITDAR results" and trends "continued through October"
Attributed claim, not tested; October is after the quarter and before the cutoff and is not covered by filed numbers.

Gaming taxes are the largest retail cost: in Q3 2026 285.8 in Northeast on revenue 708.3, 89.4 in Midwest on 341.9, 58.0 in South on 291.8, 26.3 in West on 147.5; compensation and benefits and other segment items follow
Tax rates are set by states, so margin is exposed to tax increases; the Northeast gaming-tax ratio is 40.3%.
The majority of land and buildings is leased under triple net master leases, mainly with GLPI (AR PENN, 2023 and Pinnacle Master Leases) and VICI (VICI Master Lease from December 4, 2025)
Rent is a fixed and escalating claim; operating lease rent expense is 494.4 for nine months 2026, and cash payments to landlords 746.6.

OSB, iCasino and social gaming, management of retail sportsbooks, and the theScore media app (approximately 4 million monthly active users); market access agreements with operators in six states; Alberta launch July 13, 2026
Documentary Fact; Alberta launch from release
Market access partners pay a gaming tax reimbursement that is booked as revenue and cost; profit depends on marketing spend and iCasino growth.

Online gaming revenue decreased as iCasino growth was offset by lower OSB handle; Interactive Adjusted EBITDA loss was 18.3 in Q3 2026 against 76.6 and 38.7 for nine months against 227.6, driven by lower marketing, general and administrative and labor costs
Improvement is from cost cuts after the ESPN agreement ended; revenue ex gross-up is flat to lower, so durability depends on keeping costs low.

2026 anticipated maintenance capital 220.0 and project capital 170.0, of which 111.5 and 139.7 incurred in nine months; each Triple Net Lease other than Morgantown requires spending a minimum of 1% of annual net revenues on maintenance
Part of capex is contractually required; project capex is discretionary and partly funded by GLPI sale-leasebacks.

Council Bluffs relocation 180.0 to 200.0 expected to open in 2028 with GLPI committed to finance up to 150.0 at a 7.1% cap rate; New Orleans relocation about 195.0 expected to open in 2029, financed from cash on hand but with balance sheet access possible
Each GLPI-funded project adds fixed rent; self-funded projects consume liquidity.
Working capital metrics (receivable and payable days, deposits) are Not disclosed as measures; the cash-flow statement shows accrued expenses and prepaid movements
Cannot assess working-capital cash conversion beyond the statement lines.
Operations are subject to seasonality from weather, holidays, events and sporting calendars
Quarterly liquidity can swing; the 2026-09-30 cash balance is not a minimum.

Competes with other casinos, state lotteries, sweepstakes, video gaming terminals, illegal slots and skill games and emerging prediction markets; new supply and weather weighed on the South segment in the first quarter of 2026
New supply and substitute products are a risk to retail visitation in specific markets.
PENN Play loyalty program with over 34 million members; concentration of revenue by customer or property is Not disclosed in the pages read
Loyalty drives cross-sell; property-level concentration cannot be assessed.

runs.text: Strengths. Liquidity and refinancing runway [Documentary Fact]: PENN holds cash of USD 1,044.8 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 976.1 million maturing April 2031, so liquidity of USD 2,020.9 million covers the USD 432.3 million of twelve-month maturities several times over, and bank maturities now sit in 2031 and 2033 [CP-1 Chart data: liquidity; CP-1A Transaction summary and new debt issues]. Deleveraging on management measures [Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]: total debt fell to USD 2,806.6 million from USD 2,904.1 million while LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 1,088.2 million, giving 2.58x gross and 1.62x net, which lowers the burden of the floating term loans and eases refinancing [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. Retail earnings power [Documentary Fact]: Segment Adjusted EBITDAR of USD 501.8 million in Q3 2026 on a 33.7% margin, spread across 28 jurisdictions and 42 gaming and racing properties, supports cash flow from a diversified base [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A Company and operating model]. Governance record [Analyst Interpretation]: no priming, uptier, drop-down or collateral release was found, buybacks of USD 354.4 million in FY2025 stopped in nine months 2026, and the February 2026 activist settlement removed an open contest, which is supportive of creditors though the debt documents that would constrain future behaviour are not supplied [CP-1A Ownership, governance and capital allocation].

Weaknesses. Landlord obligations [Documentary Fact for amounts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]: lease and financing obligations of USD 8,157.6 million sit outside the debt figure, of which USD 4,359.4 million is not deducted in EBITDA, so fixed-charge leverage is far higher than the headline, and a lease default is also a debt default [CP-1 Claims outside debt; CP-1A Credit translations]. Online segment [Analyst Interpretation]: a loss of USD 18.3 million in Q3 2026 and a loss of USD 78.6 million over the LTM period mean the segment still consumes cash, and the improvement rests on cost cuts with revenue ex gross-up flat, so earnings could slip if marketing returns [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Interest burden [Documentary Fact]: cash interest of USD 382.4 million against LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,088.2 million leaves cover of 2.85x, and LTM net income was a loss of USD 11.0 million [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics]. Earnings quality [Documentary Fact]: Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back items including USD 44.9 million labelled Other for nine months 2026, so its underlying level cannot be tested against the ledger [CP-1 Quality and definition notes on EBITDA]. Information gaps [Insufficient Information]: covenant ratios, guarantor identity, restricted-payment capacity, large-holder data and ratings are not supplied, which prevents a view on headroom and creditor protections and limits confidence to Medium [CP-0; CP-1A Gaps].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: There is no change-of-control, acquisition or sponsor transaction in the period, and no transaction source for one; the transaction rows below are financing and development events. On March 16, 2026 PENN issued 600.0 of 6.75% senior unsecured notes at par due April 1, 2031, callable from April 1, 2028 at declining premiums, interest payable each April 1 and October 1; the notes are not guaranteed by subsidiaries unless certain subsidiary-guaranteed debt securities are later issued, and net proceeds repaid revolver borrowings (10-Q Q3 page:18). Issuance costs were 10.3. On April 16, 2026 the Third Amendment refinanced and extended the 1.0 billion revolver and the 446.9 Term Loan A to April 2031, removed the credit spread adjustment, with margins of 1.50% to 2.25% over Term SOFR (10-Q Q3 page:17). On May 28, 2026 the Fourth Amendment extended the 962.5 Term Loan B to May 2033 and cut margins by 50 basis points to 2.00% over Term SOFR, with a SOFR floor of 0.50% (page:18); issuance costs of 16.3 and an original issue discount of 2.4 were recorded for the two amendments. In May 2026 the remaining 106.7 of the 2.75% convertible notes was repaid at maturity. The result at 2026-09-30 is total debt principal of 2806.6 (CP-1), with the nearest large maturity the 400.0 5.625% Notes due January 15, 2027 which are classified long-term on the Company's "intent and ability to refinance on a long-term basis" (page:19).

Use of proceeds and liquidity effect: the notes repaid revolver drawings, lifting undrawn revolver capacity; the amendments extended maturities; the Aurora sale-leaseback brought in 216.3 of GLPI funding on June 24, 2026 against 225.0 committed, adding 17.4 of annual rent. These events are described as completed, not proposed. Status of proposed items: the Council Bluffs financing by GLPI of up to 150.0 is a commitment at PENN's request and not yet drawn or leased; the New Orleans project is planned. After the quarter and before the cutoff (subsequent events): on October 15, 2026 the Company gave notice to redeem all exchangeable shares for common stock on or about December 15, 2026, and fixed rent under the AR PENN Master Lease rose by 4.4 on November 1, 2026 (10-Q Q3 pages 21 and 31). No new debt issue after 2026-09-30 and no rating action is in the supplied text.

Third, the improvement in EBITDA depends on the Interactive segment, whose loss narrowed to 18.3 in Q3 2026 but which remains negative, and the Q3 2025 comparison is flattered by the absence of ESPN-related advertising of 52.0 (37.5 under the Sportsbook Agreement and 14.5 under the Investment Agreement, 10-Q Q3 page:41) that was in Q3 2025 media and advertising expense; the 825.0 Q3 2025 impairment distorts net income but not Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, which adds impairment back.

fields.value: PENN is a public company without a sponsor or controlling holder disclosed in the supplied text. It runs regional casinos and racetracks and an online sports betting and iCasino business across North America, and its real estate sits mostly with landlords under long-dated triple net leases. For a creditor the structure matters more than the brand: the retail segments produce the cash flow, rent is a fixed and escalating operating cost paid before debt service and a lease default is also a debt default, and the Interactive segment is moving toward break-even by cutting cost rather than by growing underlying revenue. The 2026 transactions were refinancings and development financings rather than a change of control: a new 600.0 unsecured note, extended bank maturities, and sale-leaseback funding from GLPI for the Aurora project. The history that matters is the 2023 Barstool round trip, the 2023 to 2025 ESPN relationship and its early end, the 2025 to 2026 activist contest settled by a cooperation agreement, and the shift from buybacks in 2025 to none in 2026. Creditor protections in the credit agreement and indentures, board composition detail and large-holder data are not supplied, so legal capacity to pay out cash, incur debt or release collateral is not assessed and the governance read relies on documented actions only.

On March 16, 2026 PENN issued 600.0 of 6.75% senior unsecured notes at par due April 1, 2031, callable from April 1, 2028 at declining premiums, interest payable each April 1 and October 1; the notes are not guaranteed by subsidiaries unless certain subsidiary-guaranteed debt securities are later issued, and net proceeds repaid revolver borrowings (10-Q Q3 page:18). Issuance costs were 10.3. On April 16, 2026 the Third Amendment refinanced and extended the 1.0 billion revolver and the 446.9 Term Loan A to April 2031, removed the credit spread adjustment, with margins of 1.50% to 2.25% over Term SOFR (10-Q Q3 page:17). On May 28, 2026 the Fourth Amendment extended the 962.5 Term Loan B to May 2033 and cut margins by 50 basis points to 2.00% over Term SOFR, with a SOFR floor of 0.50% (page:18); issuance costs of 16.3 and an original issue discount of 2.4 were recorded for the two amendments. In May 2026 the remaining 106.7 of the 2.75% convertible notes was repaid at maturity. The result at 2026-09-30 is total debt principal of 2806.6 (CP-1), with the nearest large maturity the 400.0 5.625% Notes due January 15, 2027 which are classified long-term on the Company's "intent and ability to refinance on a long-term basis" (page:19).

fields.value: 1. Landlord claims and cross-default. Evidence: the AR PENN and 2023 Master Leases are "cross-defaulted, cross-collateralized, and coterminous, and subject to a parent guarantee" (10-Q Q3 page:21), and a default under a master lease "could result in a default under our debt agreements" (10-K page:35). Risk mechanic: a lease default or termination removes operating properties and accelerates debt through cross-default, so lease performance gates the whole capital structure. Credit implication: lease coverage and rent escalation are first-order credit drivers alongside debt leverage; GLPI funding of development raises fixed rent (analyst arithmetic: 10.1, 11.7 and 17.4 of added annual rent on 130.0, 150.0 and 216.3 of funding, or 7.9% on 496.3 in total). Credit implication: refinancing risk is low in the next twelve months on liquidity but depends on market access for the 2027 and 2029 notes; the term loans are floating (weighted-average rates of 6.600% to 6.941% across maturity buckets, 10-Q Q3 page:78). Risk mechanic: the segment's improved result rests on cost removal after the ESPN agreement ended and may not persist if marketing returns to win share, while revenue ex gross-up is flat. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PENN's fundamental credit profile is improving but still burdened by landlord obligations, so the view is constructive on liquidity and refinancing and cautious on fixed charges. The strongest support is liquidity of USD 2,020.9 million and net debt of 1.62x LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,088.2 million, with bank maturities pushed to 2031 and 2033. The weakest point is that USD 8,157.6 million of lease and financing obligations sit outside debt and cross-default into the debt agreements, and that the online segment still loses money. What decides the outcome is whether the retail margin gains and online cost savings hold while rent escalates, and whether the USD 400.0 million of notes due January 15, 2027 are refinanced on acceptable terms. [CP-1; CP-1A]

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: PENN's reported leverage fell through 2026 on the company's own definition. Total debt over LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is 2.58x against 3.50x at FY2025, and net debt over EBITDA is 1.62x against 2.67x, as cash rose to USD 1,044.8 million and EBITDA rose to USD 1,088.2 million from USD 830.1 million [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. The measure is management's non-GAAP view struck after triple net operating lease rent and it leaves out USD 4,359.4 million of financing obligations and finance leases, so an extended perimeter that adds them gives net leverage of 5.63x [CP-1 Calculations]. Creditors should therefore treat the improvement as real but read the level against the landlord claims, not against the headline ratio.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is the clearest strength. Cash of USD 1,044.8 million plus an undrawn revolver of USD 976.1 million gives USD 2,020.9 million, against USD 432.3 million of debt maturing in the next twelve months and no committed facility located that expires within that period [CP-1 Chart data: liquidity; CP-1 Calculations]. The 2026 refinancing extended the revolver and Term Loan A to April 2031 and Term Loan B to May 2033 and added USD 600.0 million of 6.75% notes due 2031 [CP-1A Transaction summary and new debt issues]. The near-term maturity that remains is the USD 400.0 million of 5.625% notes due January 15, 2027, which the company classifies as long-term on its intent and ability to refinance.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The earnings recovery has two unequal sources. Retail Segment Adjusted EBITDAR was USD 501.8 million in Q3 2026 against USD 465.8 million, with the margin at 33.7% against 32.8% [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics]. The online segment's loss narrowed to USD 18.3 million from USD 76.6 million, but revenue excluding the gaming tax gross-up was USD 157.0 million against USD 158.2 million, and online gaming revenue fell, so the gain came from lower marketing, general and administrative and labor costs after the ESPN agreement ended [CP-1; CP-1A Company and operating model]. That makes part of the earnings recovery depend on keeping costs low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fixed charges remain heavy. LTM cash paid for interest of USD 382.4 million gives cash interest cover of 2.85x on LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA, up from 2.17x at FY2025 [CP-1 Chart data: interest cover]. Leases are the structural issue: the AR PENN and 2023 Master Leases are cross-defaulted and a master lease default could trigger a default under the debt agreements, and the development funding GLPI provides adds annual rent of about 7.9% of the funds received [CP-1A Credit translations]. Covenant headroom is not measurable: the maximum total net leverage of 4.50x and minimum interest coverage of 2.00x are printed but the reported ratios and definitions are not supplied [CP-1 Covenants].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Liquidity and refinancing runway [Documentary Fact]: PENN holds cash of USD 1,044.8 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 976.1 million maturing April 2031, so liquidity of USD 2,020.9 million covers the USD 432.3 million of twelve-month maturities several times over, and bank maturities now sit in 2031 and 2033 [CP-1 Chart data: liquidity; CP-1A Transaction summary and new debt issues]. Deleveraging on management measures [Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]: total debt fell to USD 2,806.6 million from USD 2,904.1 million while LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 1,088.2 million, giving 2.58x gross and 1.62x net, which lowers the burden of the floating term loans and eases refinancing [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. Retail earnings power [Documentary Fact]: Segment Adjusted EBITDAR of USD 501.8 million in Q3 2026 on a 33.7% margin, spread across 28 jurisdictions and 42 gaming and racing properties, supports cash flow from a diversified base [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A Company and operating model]. Governance record [Analyst Interpretation]: no priming, uptier, drop-down or collateral release was found, buybacks of USD 354.4 million in FY2025 stopped in nine months 2026, and the February 2026 activist settlement removed an open contest, which is supportive of creditors though the debt documents that would constrain future behaviour are not supplied [CP-1A Ownership, governance and capital allocation].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Landlord obligations [Documentary Fact for amounts, Analyst Interpretation for the reading]: lease and financing obligations of USD 8,157.6 million sit outside the debt figure, of which USD 4,359.4 million is not deducted in EBITDA, so fixed-charge leverage is far higher than the headline, and a lease default is also a debt default [CP-1 Claims outside debt; CP-1A Credit translations]. Online segment [Analyst Interpretation]: a loss of USD 18.3 million in Q3 2026 and a loss of USD 78.6 million over the LTM period mean the segment still consumes cash, and the improvement rests on cost cuts with revenue ex gross-up flat, so earnings could slip if marketing returns [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Interest burden [Documentary Fact]: cash interest of USD 382.4 million against LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of USD 1,088.2 million leaves cover of 2.85x, and LTM net income was a loss of USD 11.0 million [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics]. Earnings quality [Documentary Fact]: Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back items including USD 44.9 million labelled Other for nine months 2026, so its underlying level cannot be tested against the ledger [CP-1 Quality and definition notes on EBITDA]. Information gaps [Insufficient Information]: covenant ratios, guarantor identity, restricted-payment capacity, large-holder data and ratings are not supplied, which prevents a view on headroom and creditor protections and limits confidence to Medium [CP-0; CP-1A Gaps].

This module traces the claims in the readiness, financial, business and synthesis handoffs back to the seven pinned sources, recomputes their arithmetic, checks them against one another, and grades the run. fields.value: Each handoff was opened and compared with the sources, not only with the other handoffs. Where this handoff differs from an earlier one it says so and gives the corrected statement; the earlier handoff stays as accepted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Every material claim in the four handoffs was traced to a located source span, and the arithmetic was recomputed from the cited figures. The headline financial claims hold: debt principal of 2,806.6 and cash of 1,044.8 at 2026-09-30, liquidity of 2,020.9, LTM Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA of 1,088.2, and the ratios derived from them, all recompute exactly and share one perimeter and period basis. A set of 186 figure and phrase checks against the cited pages found 179 at the cited location; the other 7 were examined individually and two were real locator errors, the rest check-string artifacts or an adjacent page already cited. The audit found six issues, all minor: wrong page numbers for three cash-flow lines and one working-capital reference, a statement that gaming taxes are the largest retail cost that is true for only two of four retail segments, a landlord-payment figure of 252.2 that should read 263.3, a gap for the 4.125% notes that the 10-K fills, and a cross-default described more broadly than the filing supports in two handoffs. None changes a ratio, a liquidity figure or the direction of the credit view, so the run is graded Passed with corrections logged. The strongest contrary reading is that the improvement is overstated: the company's debt measure leaves out financing obligations and finance leases of 4,359.4 and LTM net income is a loss of 11.0, so the handoffs already carry the extended-perimeter leverage of 5.63x. What would make the contrary view win is covenant definitions that count those obligations as debt, which the missing credit agreement prevents anyone from testing.
